name: Shibuya
tagline: Shibuya in 1 minute and Shinjuku in 5 minutes. Served by 10 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥150,000 to ¥160,000.
summary: The station is in Shibuya City, where JR East, Keio, Tokyu and Tokyo Metro run 10 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 19 minutes to Otemachi, 5 minutes to Shinjuku, 1 minute to Shibuya and 21 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥150,000 to ¥160,000. The station stands 15.1 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 20.7 m. The land around the station rises and falls sharply.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 15.1 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 10.6 m to 31.3 m, a difference of 20.7 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls outside the projected inundation area. Even so, 2 of the nine points within 400 m fall inside the area, and the deepest projection there is 0.5 to 3 m. On the whole, the flood projection here is among the smallest in the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 26 clinics and 24 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 衣笠眼科, about 2 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 湘南美容外科, about 4 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 10 lines serve the station. JR Yamanote Line and JR Saikyo Line run through it. Narita Express and JR Shonan-Shinjuku Line also call here. Keio Inokashira Line and Tokyu Toyoko Line are available too. Tokyu Den-en-toshi Line stop here as well. Tokyo Metro Ginza Line stop here as well. Tokyo Metro Hanzomon Line stop here as well. Tokyo Metro Fukutoshin Line stop here as well. The lines are split between operators (JR East runs 4 lines, Keio runs 1 line, Tokyu runs 2 lines and Tokyo Metro runs 3 lines), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company.
congestion: JR Saikyo Line runs at 167% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 板橋→池袋, which this station is not on. Tokyo Metro Ginza Line runs at 153%. Its busiest stretch is 赤坂見附→溜池山王, which this station is likewise not on. Tokyu Den-en-toshi Line runs at 138% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch of the line is 池尻大橋→渋谷, which includes this station. Narita Express and JR Shonan-Shinjuku Line is not covered by the ministry's congestion survey. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥150,000 to ¥160,000 and 1K ¥140,000 to ¥150,000. 1LDK ¥270,000 to ¥280,000 and 2LDK ¥460,000 to ¥470,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.
drivers: Age and construction of the building
Whether it faces a main road or the railway
Whether it sits at the top or the bottom of a slope

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥150,000 to ¥160,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the high side. 10 lines and a wide choice of connections and a small projected flood depth pushes the figure up. On the other side, a climb from the station to much of the housing holds it down. For 1LDK, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: For quiet, Shinsen; for rail connections, Shibuya.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Shibuya. Shinsen has only the Keio Inokashira Line, so Shibuya is the better connected. To Toranomon, for instance, Shinsen takes 7 minutes longer. On quiet, though, Shinsen comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: For quiet, Meiji-Jingumae; for rail connections, Shibuya.
neighbours.note: About 1 km from Shibuya in a straight line. Meiji-Jingumae has only the JR Yamanote Line, Tokyo Metro Chiyoda Line and Tokyo Metro Fukutoshin Line, so Shibuya is the better connected. To Shinagawa, for instance, Meiji-Jingumae takes 8 minutes longer. On quiet, though, Meiji-Jingumae comes out ahead.

goodFor: People commuting to Otemachi and Marunouchi
People who want another route when a line stops
notFor: People who would rather not walk up and down slopes
People who want to hold the rent down
noiseSources: The 首都高速3号渋谷線 viaduct runs just outside the station. It is an expressway, so traffic is audible day and night
明治通り (a main road) runs right beside the station, so for a flat close to the station, check whether it faces the road

leads.terrain: The ground around the station rises and falls sharply, and living above or below the slope changes how much effort getting about takes.
leads.groceries: There are 10 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 3 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself is outside the projected flood area, but blocks nearby are inside it.
leads.stationNote: 10 lines serve the station, and the choice of connections is wider than at most stations in the 23 wards.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the high side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is among the highest in the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are some of the most heavily loaded in the morning.
leads.noiseSources: At this station, check the traffic noise before the noise people make.
